historyTimeline.h2: Mitsubishi Shogun Pajero 2.5 TD - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mitsubishi Shogun Pajero 2.5 TD (4D56/4D56T) arrived as a core diesel option in the first-generation Shogun/Pajero (L040 series) from 1986, offering a robust and reliable turbo diesel alternative to the petrol V6 variants. The 4D56 engine family continued across three generations of Shogun/Pajero (L040/V30/V70), becoming one of the most widely fitted diesel units in the Shogun range worldwide and a favourite among UK off-road enthusiasts and commercial operators for its torque-rich, low-end pulling power .

milestones.description: 4D56 2.5L naturally aspirated diesel introduced on first-generation Shogun/Pajero (L040 series), producing 74-85hp
4D56T turbocharged variant introduced, boosting output to 99-115hp; timing belt drive, SOHC 8-valve design
Second-generation Shogun/Pajero (V30 series) continues with 4D56T, refined turbo diesel with improved emissions
4M40 2.8L turbo diesel introduced alongside 4D56, offering higher torque option; 4D56 remains entry diesel
4D56T adopted in Shogun Sport (K90 series) and L200 pickup
Third-generation Shogun/Pajero (V70 series) retains 4D56T as entry diesel option
Power output reaches 114-136hp; 16-valve variants appear in some markets
4D56 production ends for Shogun range as 4M41 3.2L DI-D takes over
4D56 remains in production for export markets (Pajero Sport/L200) until 2016

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mitsubishi Shogun Pajero 2.5 TD 4D56T is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

specs.label: Power Output
specs.value: 99-115hp (UK market variants); up to 136hp on later export models

items.commonFailure: Cylinder head cracking is a well-documented issue on 4D56T engines, particularly on post-2000 production units where metallurgy changes made the flat-face head more prone to cracking . Head gasket failure (bubbles in coolant header tank) is also common . Timing belt replacement is critical - the engine has a timing belt (not a chain) and belt failure causes catastrophic valvetrain damage . Typical failure mileage for head issues: 80k-150k.

problems.h4: Cylinder Head Cracking - Why the Mitsubishi Shogun 2.5 TD 4D56T Head Fails
problems.affectedModels: Mitsubishi Shogun Pajero 2.5 TD 4D56T (1986-2006, post-2000 units especially)
problems.rootCause: The flat-face cylinder head design on 4D56T engines is prone to cracking, particularly on post-2000 production units where metallurgy changes made the head more susceptible to thermal stress. Symptoms include coolant loss, bubbles in the expansion tank, and overheating .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Pressure test, coolant flush, thermostat replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Precautionary; extends head life on high-mileage 4D56T

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace with new or reconditioned head, gasket, bolts; pressure test
repairOptions.longevity: If head crack confirmed but bottom end sound; most cost-effective option

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit full rebuilt 4D56T engine, warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If head failure caused overheating and bottom-end damage, or if mileage justifies full rebuild

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Mitsubishi Shogun Pajero 2.5 TD of relevant age (1986-2006) sits in the £3,000-£12,000 band depending on condition, mileage, and generation `[INDUSTRY ESTIMATE]`. A full rebuilt 4D56T at £2,200-£2,800 plus fitting sits at around 30-50% of vehicle value on mid-range examples, making replacement viable but worthy of careful evaluation. For pre-1995 Shogun 2.5 TD examples worth under £4,000, consider used engine options or evaluate scrap value first.
problems.recommendation: If your Shogun 2.5 TD 4D56T has bubbles in the header tank or evidence of coolant loss, get a compression test and cylinder head inspection immediately. Catching head cracking early can save the bottom end. A new or reconditioned cylinder head at £800-£1,500 is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement, and on a well-maintained 4D56T, the bottom end can outlast multiple heads. For post-2000 units with known metallurgy issues, consider preventative head replacement at 100k if you're keeping the vehicle long-term.

problems.h4: Timing Belt Failure - Catastrophic Damage Prevention for 4D56T
problems.typicalFailureMileage: If not replaced at 60k-80k intervals, belt failure causes terminal engine damage
problems.rootCause: The 4D56 engine family uses a timing belt, not a chain . If the belt snaps, pistons hit valves, bending them and damaging the head - catastrophic engine failure requiring full rebuild or replacement.

repairOptions.longevity: Standard service at 60k-80k intervals; essential maintenance

repairOptions.tier: Full rebuild - after timing belt snap
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip and inspect; replace bent valves, damaged pistons, head; often requires full rebuild
repairOptions.longevity: If belt snapped; assess whether engine is worth rebuilding
If timing belt failure caused severe engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Mitsubishi Shogun Pajero 2.5 TD sits in the £3,000-£12,000 band. A timing belt replacement at £250-£450 represents excellent value - it's around 5-10% of vehicle value and prevents catastrophic engine failure. This is one of the most cost-effective preventative maintenance items on any 4D56T.
problems.recommendation: If you don't know the timing belt history on your Shogun 2.5 TD 4D56T, replace it immediately. The 4D56 uses a timing belt with a recommended 60k-80k-mile replacement interval - and unlike chain-driven engines, belt failure is terminal . This is one of the few cases where a preventative repair is always cheaper than waiting for failure. For high-mileage 4D56T engines, include the balance shaft belt and tensioner in the service - balance shaft issues are also documented on these engines and can cause vibration .

problems.group: Fuel Injection Pump and Injector Issues
problems.h4: Fuel Injection Pump and Injector Issues - Erratic Idle and Black Smoke
problems.affectedModels: Mitsubishi Shogun Pajero 2.5 TD 4D56T (1996-2006, common on Shogun Sport and L200 variants)
problems.rootCause: The 4D56T uses a rotary injection pump. Pump wear causes overfuelling symptoms including black smoke, erratic idle, and revs sticking at 1,200-3,000rpm on lift-off. Fuel pump failure can occur without EML illumination, making diagnosis difficult .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Injector leak-off test, fuel pump pressure test, air leak check on inlet side
repairOptions.longevity: First step; air leaks on inlet side can cause similar symptoms

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Refurbish or replace injectors; test spray pattern

repairOptions.tier: Fuel injection pump replacement or refurb
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace or refurbish rotary injection pump; recalibrate
repairOptions.longevity: If pump wear confirmed; common cause of overfuelling on 4D56T
If pump failure caused contamination or engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Shogun Pajero 2.5 TD sits in the £3,000-£12,000 band. Fuel injection pump replacement at £700-£1,200 is 15-25% of vehicle value on older examples - weigh against overall vehicle condition and mileage.
problems.recommendation: Start with diagnostics - many Shogun 2.5 TD owners chase pump issues only to find an air leak on the inlet side causing similar symptoms . Blank off the EGR valve and check all vacuum pipes, as EGR issues are also common on high-mileage 4D56T engines. If diagnostics confirm pump wear, a refurbished pump with warranty from a diesel specialist offers the best value - full engine replacement is rarely justified for pump failure alone.

items.question: What are the signs of 4D56T engine failure in a Shogun 2.5 TD?
items.answer: Common warning signs include bubbles in the coolant header tank (head gasket or head crack), black smoke and erratic idle (fuel pump or injector wear), and timing belt age (preventative replacement critical).
keyPoints: Coolant loss + bubbles -> head gasket or cylinder head crack - most common on post-2000 4D56T units
Black smoke + revs sticking -> fuel pump or injector issues; check inlet air leaks first
No recorded timing belt change -> immediate preventative replacement at 60k-80k miles
items.cta: -> Need a 4D56T diagnosis? Get specialist quotes

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mitsubishi Shogun Pajero 2.5 TD?
items.answer: A typical Shogun 2.5 TD from 1986-2006 is worth £3,000-£12,000, so a rebuilt engine at £2,200-£2,800 plus fitting represents 30-50% of vehicle value on mid-range examples. For older or lower-value examples, consider used engine options or cylinder head replacement.
keyPoints: Mid-range Shogun 2.5 TD (£6k-£10k): rebuilt engine is sensible if keeping the vehicle 2+ years
Lower-value Shogun 2.5 TD (under £4k): used engine or cylinder head repair typically makes more sense
Commercial use or off-road enthusiast vehicle: replacement often justifiable even at higher cost
items.cta: -> Compare your Shogun 2.5 TD engine replacement options

items.question: Does the Mitsubishi Shogun 2.5 TD (4D56T) have a timing belt or chain?
items.answer: The 4D56/4D56T engine uses a timing belt, not a chain . That means scheduled timing belt replacement is critical - the recommended interval is 60,000 miles. If the belt breaks, pistons hit valves causing catastrophic engine damage.
keyPoints: Timing belt replacement at 60k-80k miles is mandatory on 4D56T
Include tensioner and idler pulleys in the kit
Balance shaft belt replacement is also recommended on high-mileage engines
items.cta: -> Check your Shogun 2.5 TD 4D56T timing belt history

items.question: What's the difference between the 4D56 and 4D56T engines in the Shogun?
items.answer: The 4D56 is the naturally aspirated 2.5L diesel fitted to early first-generation Shoguns (1986-1990), producing 74-85hp. The 4D56T is the turbocharged version fitted to most UK-market 2.5 TD Shoguns, producing 99-115hp and offering significantly better torque and drivability .
keyPoints: 4D56: naturally aspirated, 74-85hp, rarer in UK Shoguns
4D56T: turbocharged, 99-115hp, the common UK 2.5 TD engine
Both share the same 2.5L block, timing belt, and head cracking vulnerability
